items.title: Hyperfiniteness on the set covered infinitely often by separated Borel sets of a bounded-degree decomposition
items.author: Balázs Bursics; Zoltán Vidnyánszky
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem t:separation2 at source lines 425-430: an increasing sequence of bounded-degree Borel graphs G_n covering a CBER E, a scale f with f(n+1) >= 2(f(n)+1), and Borel sets B_n that are f(n)-separated in G_n jointly force E restricted to B, where B is the set of points lying in infinitely many B_n, to be hyperfinite. The construction H_{n+1} = H_n union the G_{n+1}-edges inside B meeting B_{n+1} (source line 593) is one line, but the diameter bound is not: the inner Claim at lines 597-606 first has to exclude two points of B_{n+1} in one component of H_{n+1} by routing the interior of a shortest path through a single component of H_n and applying the induction hypothesis, which yields dist_{G_{n+1}}(x,x') <= f(n)+2 <= f(n+1) against the separation of B_{n+1} (line 602). The remaining vertices are then one H_n-component per G_{n+1}-neighbour of the single B_{n+1}-point, giving diam(H) <= 2(f(n)+1) <= f(n+1) (lines 604-605). The factor 2 with the +1 offset is what makes this induction close, so neither a bounded-degree counting argument alone nor a direct matching decomposition of E restricted to B reaches the conclusion.
